Melting Practice Carbon and Low Alloy Steel - Electric furnace (EF) or basic 
oxygen furnace shall be acceptable steel melting practices. Any additional 
processing such as argon oxygen decarburization (AOD), electroslag re-melting 
(ESR), ladle refining, vacuum degassing, or vacuum arc re-melting (VAR) maybe 
be performed when required. 
Melting Practice Austenitic Stainless Steel – Two-step process consisting of 
electric furnace (EF) melting or vacuum induction melting followed by argon 
oxygen decarburization (AOD), vacuum degassing, vacuum arc re-melting (VAT) 
or electroslag re-melting (ESR). 
Grain size for Low Alloy Steels - Grain size of 5 or finer (i.e. 5 or higher 
number) per ASTM E112 is required for low alloy steels. A statement from the 
mill of ‘fine grain practice” may be used in lieu of the actual number. 
Radioactivity Free Material - Raw material melt sources shall have procedures 
in place to assure that the raw material used for bars and forgings is free from 
radioactivity.

Equipment Qualification: Heat treatment operations shall be performed with 
heat-treating equipment that satisfies one of the following; 
• 
Calibrated in accordance with API 6A section 6.5.2 and 6.5.3 and 
surveyed in accordance with API 6A Annex M and section 6.5.4.1 for 
batch type furnaces. Or; 
• 
Equipment has been calibrated and surveyed in accordance with SAE 
AMS 2750 Class 1, 2 or 3 for tempering and Class 1, 2, 3, 4 or 5 for 
normalizing and austenitizing. 
Furnaces used for continuous heat treatment shall be operated, maintained, 
modified and repaired in accordance with SAE AMS2750 or SAE AMSH6875 and 
calibrated/surveyed in accordance with API Specification 6A Annex M. 
Method for Batch Heat Treatment: The QTC shall experience the same heat 
treatment processing as the material/part(s) it qualifies. Time at temperature and 
heat treatment cycles shall comply with the specific CMS. If the QTC is not heat 
treated as part of the same heat treatment lot as the material/part(s) it qualifies, 
the austenitizing, solution treating, or age hardening (as applicable) 
temperatures for the QTC shall be within 25F (14C) of those for the 
material/part(s). The tempering temperature of the material/part(s) shall not be 
lower than 25F (14C) below that of the QTC. The upper limit shall be no higher 
than that permitted by the specific CMS. The cycle time of the QTC at each 
temperature shall not exceed that for the material/part(s). 
Oven shall be loaded with appropriate spacing between parts to ensure proper 
heat treatment. In no case shall parts be stacked or touching during heat 
treatment.

Composition 
An analysis of each heat of steel shall be made by the supplier, preferably from a 
ladle sample taken at or near the time of pouring. The required chemical 
elements shall be reported in weight percent. While reporting of residual 
elements is not required, unless called out in the specific CMS, the supplier must 
ensure the total residuals do not exceed 1%. Chemical composition including 
composition tolerances are stated in the specific CMS.

Continuous furnace: For material heat treated in a continuous furnace, the 
QTC shall consist of a sacrificial production part or a prolongation removed from 
the production part, the sacrificial production part or prolongation QTC shall 
qualify only production part(s) having an identical size and shape. The QTC 
shall qualify only material/part(s) produced from the same heat and heat treat lot. 
Batch-type furnace: For batch heat treatment only, if the QTC is a trepanned 
core or prolongation removed from a production part, the QTC may qualify only 
production part(s) having the same or smaller ER. The QTC shall qualify only 
material/part(s) produced from the same heat. 
Production Parts: 
 
A sacrificial production part may be usable depending on the size and 
location of the test specimen from which it is selected. 
 
For a production part with a complex shape or varying cross-section, it is not 
necessary that the prolongation be an extension of the largest cross-section 
of the part, but the extension shall meet or exceed the minimum ER required 
for a separate QTC. 
Prolongations: 
 
When a prolongation is used, it shall remain integrally attached during all 
heat-treatment operations, except post-weld heat-treatment, stress relief, and 
any re-tempering or re-aging that can be required. 
 
For tubular parts, bar stock, mill shapes, and other raw material with a 
uniform cross-section, the prolongation shall have the same cross-section as 
that of the raw material

Testing 
Heat treated material/material/part(s) and the QTC shall be hardness tested in 
accordance with procedures in ASTM E10 (Brinell) or ASTM E18 (Rockwell). 
Forgings may be Brinell hardness tested using portable hardness testers 
meeting the requirements of ASTM E110 or ASTM E10. 
At least two Rockwell or Brinell hardness test measurement shall be performed 
on the QTC after the QTC final heat treatment cycle. The QTC heat treatment 
cycles prior to hardness testing shall be the very same heat treatment cycles 
experienced by the tensile and impact test specimens. 
Welding 
Welding on the QTC is not allowed, except for attachment-type welds.

Any nondestructive examination specified by the EPS or the specific CMS shall 
be performed as the last operation prior to shipment and shall be performed in 
accordance with Cactus Wellhead NDE procedures or approved supplier NDE 
procedures.

Material shall be inspected for injurious imperfections as follows: 
 
Material in rough machined condition shall not exceed 250 AA in surface 
roughness in the machined areas and shall be free of burrs or injurious 
imperfections. 
 
Material shall be free of internal forging bursts or hydrogen flakes and have a 
workmanlike finish. 
 
Surface imperfections such as laps, seams, folds, tears, slivers, or 
mechanical marks, abrasions or pits need not be removed unless they 
infringe on the minimum wall thickness of the material or extend to a depth 
greater than 1/8 inch for forgings and 1/16 for bars.

Production Material Testing 
Each piece of production material shall be hardness tested on or near the surface using 
the Rockwell C scale method per ASTM E18 or ASTM E110, or the Brinell (10 mm ball, 
3000 kgf) method per ASTM E10 or ASTM E110 after the final heat treatment cycle. The 
surface may be prepared using light grinding. When light grinding is used it shall be to a 
maximum depth of 0.125 in. (3.18 mm). 
 
Alternatively, for each piece of production material, near surface hardness 
testing on a cross-section shall be acceptable. Near surface test shall be 0.100 
to 0.150 in. (2.54 mm to 3.81 mm) from the surface and shall be performed 
using the Rockwell C scale method per ASTM E18. 
 
For Rockwell C-scale testing, three adjacent indentations shall be made, 
averaged to calculate the mean, and the mean shall meet the hardness limit of 
this CMS. No individual hardness number may be greater than 2 HRC units 
above the maximum specified hardness number. For Brinell testing, one 
indentation is sufficient. 
 
If any Rockwell hardness requirements are not met, three additional Rockwell 
C scale indentations shall be made in the immediate area to determine new 
hardness numbers. If any Brinell hardness requirements are not met, two 
additional Brinell tests may be taken in the immediate area. If one or more of 
the re-test indentations do not meet hardness requirements of this CMS, then 
the piece is rejected. 
Qualification Test Coupon (QTC) Testing 
The QTC shall be either a prolongation (full cross-section on thickest end) or sacrificial 
production part. 
 
Cross-section hardness testing shall be performed on each QTC using the 
Rockwell C scale method per ASTM E18 or ASTM E110. For solid material, the 
center, 1/4 thickness and near surface locations shall be evaluated. For hollow 
material, the mid-wall location and both near the inner and outer surfaces shall 
be evaluated. At each location three adjacent indentations shall be performed, 
and the mean hardness number from each location shall meet the 
requirements listed above. The hardness test location for the near surface test 
shall be 0.100 - 0.150 in. (2.54 mm - 3.81 mm) from the surface. All hardness 
indentations shall be reported. No individual hardness indentation may be 
greater than 2 HRC units above the maximum specified hardness number. 
 
If any mean (average) hardness value does not meet requirements, a retest 
may be made by taking three additional indentations in the immediate area of 
the same location. Each new indentation shall meet the hardness 
requirements. The test specimen surface may be re-grounded before 
performing retesting. Only one re-grind and retest is allowed for each 
specimen. 
 
If one or more of the indentations do not meet hardness requirements of this 
CMS, then the piece is rejected.
